issues.issue: Does the Federal Court have jurisdiction to hear an appeal from an associate judge's interlocutory order refusing an extension of time to perfect the record?
issues.applicant_position: Applicants say Rule 51(1) allows appeal of associate judge orders and prevails over IRPA s.72(2)(e).
issues.respondent_position: Respondent says the order is interlocutory and not appealable under IRPA s.72(2)(e).
issues.result_quote: the Court does not have jurisdiction to hear the appeal from Associate Judge Duchesne’s interlocutory decision

issues.issue: Does an exception to the bar on appeals apply (refusal to exercise jurisdiction or jurisdictional error, per Goodman)?
issues.applicant_position: Applicants say the associate judge did not have the complete motion record, which is a jurisdictional error.
issues.respondent_position: Respondent says the burden was on applicants to file all evidence, and no jurisdictional error occurred.
issues.result_quote: The exceptions established by the Federal Court of Appeal in Goodman do not apply in this case

issues.issue: Was the associate judge right to refuse the extension of time to perfect the record under the Rule 8 / Hennelly factors? (Not reached: the Court had no jurisdiction.)
issues.applicant_position: Applicants say they needed RPD audio recordings and had a technical problem transmitting the memorandum.
issues.respondent_position: Respondent left the second motion to the Court's discretion and says the order is not appealable.
